title: The molecular gas kinematics in the host galaxy of non-repeating FRB 180924B
question: What is the molecular gas kinematic structure in the host galaxy of the non-repeating FRB 180924B, and how does it compare to the gas environments of repeating FRB host galaxies?

what.value: Spectroscopic redshift z = 0.3214, stellar mass, and star formation rate of FRB 180924B host galaxy

evidence.quote: The host is a massive spiral galaxy at $z=0.3214$ with a stellar mass of $M_{\rm \ast}=(1.32 \pm 5.1)\times 10^{9} M_\odot$ and the star formation rate (SFR) of $0.88 \pm 0.26 M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ (cite: Bannister2019; Heintz2020).

what.value: Half-light radius r_half = 0.516 arcsec (~2.5 kpc) and host galaxy centre coordinates (RA, Dec) = (21h44m25.25s, -40d54m00.81s)

evidence.quote: The CO (3-2) emission line is significantly detected at the position of the host galaxy within two-times half-light radius ($r_{\rm half}$): $r_{\rm half}=$ 0.516 arcsec $\sim$ 2.5 kpc (cite: Bhandari2020).

We utilize an aperture with a radius of 1.032 arcsec (5 kpc) centred at the host galaxy (RA, Dec)$=$ (21h44m25.25s, $-40^{\circ} 54\ensuremath{'} 00.81\ensuremath{''}$) (cite: Bhandari2020) to extract a CO spectrum of the host galaxy.

We adopted $\alpha_{\rm CO}=4.3$ $M_\odot$ (K km$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$)$^{-1}$ since the gas-phase metallicity is $12 + \log ({\rm O/H})=8.93 \pm 0.02$ (cite: Heintz2020), which is comparable to the Milky way gas-phase metallicity.

what.value: Asymmetry parameters of HI emission lines for FRB 181030A, FRB 200120E, GRB 980425, GRB 111005A, and LVHIS, HALOGAS, VIVA surveys

evidence.quote: We compare our results with the asymmetry parameters of the HI emission lines in previous works, i.e., the host galaxy of FRB 181030A, FRB200120E, the host galaxy of long gamma-ray burst (GRB) GRB 980425 and GRB 111005A (cite: Michalowski2021)
Comparison of asymmetry parameters with different galaxies (cite: Michalowski2021)

recipe.goal: Image CO(3-2) data cube and generate moment maps
recipe.method: Image calibrated visibility data using CASA tclean with Briggs robust=2.0 at ~9 km s^-1 resolution, convert to rest-frame using z=0.3214 and CO(3-2) rest frequency 345.796 GHz, and create moment 0 and moment 1 maps in CARTA
key_parameters: moment 0 integration range ~ -180 km s^-1 to ~ 110 km s^-1
assumptions: Spectroscopic redshift z = 0.3214, CO(3-2) rest frequency = 345.796 GHz

recipe.goal: Extract CO(3-2) spectrum and fit velocity components
recipe.method: Extract CO spectrum using a circular aperture centred on the host galaxy and fit double Gaussian functions to the two detected velocity components

recipe.goal: Measure peak positions and spatial offset of the two velocity components
recipe.method: Integrate each velocity component over +/- 2 sigma_V from V_sys, fit central peak positions with CASA task imfit, and compute positional uncertainty from beam major axis and S/N

recipe.goal: Derive CO luminosities and molecular gas masses
recipe.method: Calculate L'_CO(3-2) from integrated CO(3-2) line flux using Solomon & Vanden Bout (2005) equation, convert to L'_CO(1-0) via luminosity ratio, and multiply by alpha_CO to obtain M_gas
Calculate integrated flux ratio A_flux and peak flux density ratio A_peak from the best-fit Gaussian functions following Reynolds et al. (2020)
key_parameters: 20% of maximum peak height used to define V_low, V_mid, and V_high; asymmetry threshold A_flux > 1.05

answer_key.quantity: Total CO luminosity of the two velocity components

evidence.quote: The total CO luminosity (molecular-gas mass) of the two velocity components is ($2.59 \pm 0.20) \times 10^{8}$ K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$ (($2.01 \pm 0.16) \times 10^{9}$ M$_\odot$).

score_reason: Public archival single-target ALMA dataset with standard CASA pipeline calibration (version stated), clear aperture definition, explicit equations and conversion factors for luminosity, gas mass, and spectral asymmetry, though minor tclean imaging parameters and cosmological constants are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The raw data are public in the ALMA archive (2019.1.01450.S), the analysis follows a straightforward recipe (pipeline calibration, tclean with robust=2.0 at 9 km/s resolution, 1.032 arcsec aperture spectrum extraction, double-Gaussian fitting, imfit peak localization, and analytic mass/asymmetry formulas), and all key outputs are numeric.
